pr_body: Closes #5103 - [x] Depends on #9768 Adds support for displaying osu!catch-specific combo counter, with a legacy implementation **almost** matching osu!stable's implementation in terms of what's and how's displayed. Implemented this by adding a `CatchComboDisplay` component handling new and reverted judgements and is responsible of updating the skinned counter accordingly. here's a comparsion GIF to save everyone's day 😛: ([source video for better per-frame look](https://streamable.com/5aac1q)) ## Remarks - Couldn't exactly match the way osu!stable rolls down and fades its counter on miss, here's how it currently looks: - Intentionally added "hide on gameplay break" logic inside `LegacyComboCounter` instead of its parent `CatchComboDisplay` to avoid conflicting with the "hide after 1 second" transform, but can be moved if osu!lazer's combo counter animation design indicates to. - This PR may be a bit complex for review, commit-by-commit should hopefully be better in doing so. didn't want to split this into very small untestable changes.

issue_context.title: Add option for combo following catcher
issue_context.body:
In stable combo is counted right above the ryuuta/center screen ish and moves back and forth (left/right) as you move the ryuuta.  Not having this at least as an option makes ctb play feel very uncomfortable as I cannot easily tell when I've dropped a note or just see how far I've made it etc.  

This is compounded by issue #5102 making it so the only way to tell "did I just miss that?" is by looking at the top of the screen to see the combo count, which is not possible in the middle of playing any fast/difficult song
comments: This would actually require per-ruleset HUD modifications to solve this correctly.

As much as I disagree with the conclusion, I've been told per-ruleset HUD modifications aren't going to happen.

I think the way this is to be done is to duplicate the combo counter, if that's done at all.
Adding a catch-specific combo counter is definitely the way forward here. It can be done for legacy skins only to begin with.

If it makes more sense to have both (ie leave the current one but also add one above the catcher) I think that would be fine.  Having above catcher only would also be fine.

However, I think it would be a major complaint for most catch players if it wasn’t above the catcher at all though. I’m glad to hear there is potential for it to be implemented at least for legacy skins

As per [this peppy tweet](https://twitter.com/ppy/status/1281797986792509442?s=21) + this issue being open for over a year without resolution + recent complaints from others about this issue

Making a bump comment
Oh sorry, I actually missed the above comments, I'll work on this one now that the direction is clear to me.
@peppy As per the second paragraph in https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/5103#issuecomment-610232084, are you against having a combo counter above the catcher in the default osu!lazer skin?
It should only be implemented for legacy skins for now. We do not have a design for the lazer default, and there is also a completely redesign incoming so it's not a good time to make changes there.

review_comments: Was there some particular intent behind this interface? Right now it seems superfluous as it has a single implementation within the scope of this PR.
Yes, the interface is going to be used for `DefaultComboCounter` as well, also not sure if there's another way to interact with combo counter coming from the skin either way.
I think this is overengineering for one but I guess I can accept it for future usage in other rulesets. Not sure why this interface is catch-specific though; I don't think it really has to be.
Also because I didn't want to think way more ahead and expose it "for later", but I guess it's fine to move this one out as `IComboCounter`
Actually not sure about moving this one, as it asks for the combo colour of the object that was hit, which is catch-specific to my knowledge.

left it for now because there's no better way to do this for now, and it's a catch-specific interface as is for the reason above. if there was a way for `GameplayBeatmap` to relay `On{New,Revert}Result` calls this could be entirely removed.
This doesn't seem to revert completely correctly (in the miss case the judged object's colour is passed instead of `null`).
